before.label: Gender & racial formation
before.description: Examines how gender and race are historically produced through relations of power. Intersectional approaches question treating race, class, and gender separately. These exchanges do not define every strand of gender or racial-formation analysis.

before.label: Bruno Latour / laboratory studies
before.description: Studies the practical work through which scientific claims become established facts, including experiments, inscriptions, instruments, and relations among researchers. Laboratory ethnography offers a route into science studies that should not be collapsed into textual interpretation or into Bloor’s programme. The Pasteur study extends his inquiry into historical scientific change and distinguishes that analysis from an explanation by social forces alone.
before.representative_figures_and_works: With Steve Woolgar, Laboratory Life: The Social Construction of Scientific Facts (1979). The revised 1986 edition drops Social from the subtitle. Latour is one contributor within a wider field. Les Microbes: guerre et paix, suivi de Irréductions (1984; translated as The Pasteurization of France, 1988) joins historical investigation to a separate theoretical argument.

after.label: Bruno Latour / laboratory studies
after.description: Studies the practical work through which scientific claims become established facts, including experiments, inscriptions, instruments, and relations among researchers. Laboratory ethnography offers a route into science studies that should not be collapsed into textual interpretation or into Bloor’s programme. The Pasteur study extends his inquiry into historical scientific change and distinguishes that analysis from an explanation by social forces alone. Bloor’s1999response contests the treatment of sociological explanation in the Pasteur case. Law’s1986edited volume provides a particular publication context shared with Callon; collaboration does not establish agreement.

after.label: History of technology
after.description: Studies technological systems, invention, maintenance, use, and social change. Develops distinct institutions while exchanging questions with histories of science, economy, environment, and gender. Systems approaches and feminist studies of household technology show the range of its explanations. Wajcman’s feminist social-shaping questions and Bray’s Chinese domestic technologies broaden the field’s material and geographical examples.
after.representative_figures_and_works: Society for the History of Technology (1958); Technology and Culture (1959); Thomas P. Hughes, Networks of Power (1983); Ruth Schwartz Cowan, More Work for Mother (1983). Pinch and Bijker (1984) investigate technological choices; their 1987 volume with Hughes makes the exchange with STS concrete.
